# Purpose of this document

This file reorganizes the exploratory analysis around three scientific hypotheses rather than the order in which the code was written. Original stage numbers are retained in headings and in the crosswalk below. Written interpretations from the previous workflow are retained, but claims that are provisional, superseded, or not yet supported are labeled accordingly.

## Current hypotheses

**H1 — Bullfrog detection.** Site-years with independently detected bullfrogs differ in parasite richness, connectance, and modularity from site-years without bullfrog detections.

**H2 — Pond permanence.** Pond permanence predicts parasite richness and network architecture after accounting for bullfrog detection, year, and sampling effort. Permanence is treated as a habitat/hydroperiod characteristic that may interact with anthropogenic stressors, not automatically as an anthropogenic disturbance itself.

**H3 — Temporal dynamics.** Annual network dissimilarity within ponds can be partitioned into change associated with taxon turnover and change among taxa shared between years. Life-stage, drought-year, and seasonal partitions remain planned extensions rather than completed tests.

**Exploratory Bd question.** Does position in the macroparasite network correspond to Bd infection risk? This is retained as a separate exploratory branch rather than a fourth coequal hypothesis.

## Status labels

- **Core:** required for the current paper workflow.
- **Supporting/descriptive:** useful context but not the main inferential test.
- **Needs revision:** direction is relevant, but the current implementation or interpretation is not final.
- **Superseded:** replaced by a later method and retained only for provenance.
- **Deprioritized:** methodologically interpretable but weakly connected to the paper's main network questions.

## Stage crosswalk

| Original stage | Organized section | Status | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2 | Shared foundation | Core | Data cleaning, date repair, and binary edge construction |
| 3–5 | Descriptive baseline | Supporting/descriptive | Metaweb, subset metrics, and node roles |
| 5.5 | Shared utilities | Core | Reusable subnetwork construction |
| 6 | Superseded archive | Superseded | Bullfrog status inferred from parasite records |
| 8, 9.5, 9.6, 18 | Exploratory Bd branch | Supporting/deprioritized | Host-specific Bd prevalence and intensity |
| 9 | Superseded archive | Superseded | Ordinary linear models for network outcomes |
| 10 | H3 / exploratory Bd bridge | Supporting/descriptive | Host projection and Jaccard similarity |
| 11–12 | Deprioritized archive | Deprioritized / superseded | Weak Bd–macroparasite and environmental directions |
| 13 (temporal) | H3 | Supporting sensitivity analysis | Pooled/shared-site network beta diversity |
| 13 (survey status) | H1/H2 | Core | Independent bullfrog detection |
| 14–15 | H1/H2 | Core | Predictor overlap and sampling effort |
| 16 | Superseded archive | Needs revision / superseded | First GLMM pass |
| 17 | H1/H2 | Needs revision | Bipartite modularity and null comparison |
| 20 | H3 | Core | Within-site turnover versus rewiring |
| 21 | H2 support | Optional supporting | Cleaner site-year pond covariates |
| 22 | Shared diagnostics | Core | Model validation utilities |
| 23 | H1/H2 | Core, unresolved | Correct parasite-richness sampling frame |
| 24 | H1/H2 | Core, unresolved | Validated connectance model |

## 1.4 Stage 2 — Construct the master host–parasite interaction table

**Status:** Core.

An edge represents at least one observed host–parasite association for a host species at a site in a year. The edge is binary after collapsing individual dissections; it is not an abundance-weighted transmission edge.

```{r stage-02-edge-table}
#stage 2: construct master host–parasite interaction table

#cleaning disssection data

dissect_clean <- amphib_dissect %>%
  select(
    dissect_code,
    site_code,
    spp_code,
    collect_date,
    year,
    parasites
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(dissect_code),
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(spp_code),
    !is.na(year)
  )

#cleaning parasite
parasite_clean <- amphib_parasite %>%
  select(
    dissect_code,
    parasite_name,
    parasite_cnt,
    presence
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    parasite_name = str_trim(parasite_name)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(dissect_code),
    !is.na(parasite_name),
    parasite_name != ""
  )

#joining parasite obs to host metadata
hp_raw <- parasite_clean %>%
  left_join(
    dissect_clean,
    by = "dissect_code"
  )

hp_raw <- hp_raw %>% #removing incomplete obs
  filter(
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(spp_code),
    !is.na(year)
  )

#convert to binary presence
hp_binary <- hp_raw %>%
mutate(
  interaction = case_when(
    !is.na(parasite_cnt) & parasite_cnt > 0 ~ 1L,
    presence %in% c(TRUE, "Y", "Yes", 1) ~ 1L,
    TRUE ~ 0L
  )
)


#collapse to unique interactions (same host with the same site/year are collapsed into one)
hp_edges <- hp_binary %>%
  group_by(
    site_code,
    year,
    spp_code,
    parasite_name
  ) %>%
  summarize(
    interaction = max(interaction),
    n_hosts_examined = n_distinct(dissect_code),
    total_parasites = sum(parasite_cnt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(interaction == 1)


#inc. pond longevity
hp_edges <- hp_edges %>%
  left_join(
    site_info %>%
      select(site_code, longevity),
    by = "site_code"
  )

#sanity checking
cat("\nUnique interactions:", nrow(hp_edges), "\n")

cat("\nHost species:", n_distinct(hp_edges$spp_code), "\n")

cat("Parasite taxa:", n_distinct(hp_edges$parasite_name), "\n")

cat("Sites:", n_distinct(hp_edges$site_code), "\n")

cat("Years:", n_distinct(hp_edges$year), "\n")#thank god they're all reasonable

# interactions per year
hp_edges %>%
  count(year)

# interactions by longevity class
hp_edges %>%
  count(longevity)

# host richness by site
hp_edges %>%
  distinct(site_code, spp_code) %>%
  count(site_code, name = "host_richness")

# parasite richness by site
hp_edges %>%
  distinct(site_code, parasite_name) %>%
  count(site_code, name = "parasite_richness")
```

# 2. Descriptive baseline shared by all hypotheses

These stages characterize the pooled system and establish the objects reused by H1–H3. They are descriptive; pooled differences are not treated as replicated inferential evidence.

## 2.1 Stage 3 — Pooled metaweb

**Status:** Supporting/descriptive. Louvain modularity generated here is exploratory and is replaced by the bipartite method in Stage 17 for final modularity claims.

```{r stage-03-metaweb}
#stage 3: build metaweb

#creating binary edge list
meta_edges <- hp_edges %>%
  distinct(
    spp_code,
    parasite_name
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    from = paste0("host_", spp_code),
    to   = paste0("parasite_", parasite_name),
    weight = 1
  )

#creating node table
host_nodes <- meta_edges %>%
  distinct(from) %>%
  transmute(
    name = from,
    type = "Host",
    label = str_remove(from, "^host_")
  )

parasite_nodes <- meta_edges %>%
  distinct(to) %>%
  transmute(
    name = to,
    type = "Parasite",
    label = str_remove(to, "^parasite_")
  )

nodes <- bind_rows(
  host_nodes,
  parasite_nodes
)

#building graph + diagnostics
g_meta <- graph_from_data_frame(
  d = meta_edges %>%
    select(from, to, weight),
  vertices = nodes,
  directed = FALSE
)

cat("Nodes:", vcount(g_meta), "\n")
cat("Edges:", ecount(g_meta), "\n\n")

table(V(g_meta)$type)

is_bipartite(g_meta)

igraph::components(g_meta)$no


#degree dist
node_degree <- tibble(
  node = igraph::V(g_meta)$name,
  type = igraph::V(g_meta)$type,
  degree = igraph::degree(g_meta)
)

host_degree <- node_degree %>%
  filter(type == "Host") %>%
  arrange(desc(degree))

parasite_degree <- node_degree %>%
  filter(type == "Parasite") %>%
  arrange(desc(degree))

host_degree

parasite_degree


#viz 
set.seed(6262026)

V(g_meta)$bipartite_type <- V(g_meta)$type == "Host"

table(V(g_meta)$type, V(g_meta)$bipartite_type)

ggraph(g_meta, layout = "bipartite", types = V(g_meta)$bipartite_type) +
  geom_edge_link(
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    aes(color = type),
    size = 4
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Binary Host–Parasite Metaweb"
  )

#centrality
meta_centrality <- tibble(
  node = V(g_meta)$name,
  type = V(g_meta)$type,
  degree = degree(g_meta),
  betweenness = betweenness(
    g_meta,
    normalized = TRUE
  ),
  eigen = eigen_centrality(g_meta)$vector
)

meta_centrality %>%
  arrange(desc(eigen))


#host richness
host_richness <- hp_edges %>%
  distinct(
    spp_code,
    parasite_name
  ) %>%
  count(
    spp_code,
    name = "parasite_richness"
  ) 

host_richness %>%
  arrange(desc(parasite_richness))


#parasite host breadth
parasite_breadth <- hp_edges %>%
  distinct(
    spp_code,
    parasite_name
  ) %>%
  count(
    parasite_name,
    name = "host_breadth"
  ) 

parasite_breadth %>%
  arrange(desc(host_breadth))
```

## 2.2 Stage 4 — Network summaries by year and pond permanence

**Status:** Supporting/descriptive. The annual and permanence-pooled networks provide context for H2 and H3 but should not be interpreted as replicated tests.

```{r stage-04-network-subsets}

# STAGE 4: Network-level metrics for subsets

# Function to build an igraph object from an interaction table

build_hp_graph <- function(edge_df) {

  edges <- edge_df |>
    dplyr::distinct(spp_code, parasite_name) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      from = paste0("host_", spp_code),
      to = paste0("parasite_", parasite_name),
      weight = 1
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(from, to, weight)

  nodes <- tibble::tibble(
    name = unique(c(edges$from, edges$to))
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      node_type = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(name, "^host_") ~ "Host",
        stringr::str_detect(name, "^parasite_") ~ "Parasite",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      bipartite_type = node_type == "Host"
    )

  igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
    d = edges,
    vertices = nodes,
    directed = FALSE
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Function to calculate network-level metrics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

summarize_hp_graph <- function(g, subset_type, subset_value) {

  node_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
    node = igraph::V(g)$name,
    node_type = igraph::V(g)$node_type
  )

  n_hosts <- node_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(node_type == "Host") |>
    nrow()

  n_parasites <- node_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(node_type == "Parasite") |>
    nrow()

  n_edges <- igraph::ecount(g)

  possible_edges <- n_hosts * n_parasites

  connectance <- ifelse(
    possible_edges > 0,
    n_edges / possible_edges,
    NA_real_
  )

  comps <- igraph::components(g)

  giant_component_size <- max(comps$csize)

  giant_component_fraction <-
    giant_component_size / igraph::vcount(g)

  modularity_value <- if (
    igraph::ecount(g) > 0 &&
    igraph::vcount(g) > 2
  ) {
    igraph::modularity(
      igraph::cluster_louvain(g)
    )
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }

  tibble::tibble(
    subset_type = subset_type,
    subset_value = subset_value,
    n_hosts = n_hosts,
    n_parasites = n_parasites,
    n_nodes = igraph::vcount(g),
    n_edges = n_edges,
    connectance = connectance,
    mean_degree = mean(igraph::degree(g)),
    modularity = modularity_value,
    n_components = comps$no,
    giant_component_size = giant_component_size,
    giant_component_fraction = giant_component_fraction
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Pooled metaweb summary
# ------------------------------------------------------------

g_meta <- build_hp_graph(hp_edges)

summary_meta <- summarize_hp_graph(
  g = g_meta,
  subset_type = "pooled",
  subset_value = "all_years"
)

summary_meta


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Year-specific summaries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

yearly_network_summary <- hp_edges |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::group_split() |>
  purrr::map_dfr(function(df_year) {

    yr <- unique(df_year$year)

    g_year <- build_hp_graph(df_year)

    summarize_hp_graph(
      g = g_year,
      subset_type = "year",
      subset_value = as.character(yr)
    )
  })

yearly_network_summary


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Pond-longevity summaries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

longevity_network_summary <- hp_edges |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(longevity),
    longevity != ""
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(longevity) |>
  dplyr::group_split() |>
  purrr::map_dfr(function(df_longevity) {

    lon <- unique(df_longevity$longevity)

    g_longevity <- build_hp_graph(df_longevity)

    summarize_hp_graph(
      g = g_longevity,
      subset_type = "longevity",
      subset_value = as.character(lon)
    )
  })

longevity_network_summary


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Combine all summaries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

network_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  summary_meta,
  yearly_network_summary,
  longevity_network_summary
)

network_summary
```

## 2.3 Stage 5 — Node-level roles

**Status:** Supporting/descriptive.

```{r stage-05-node-metrics}
#stage 5: node level metrics

#function for node centality per graph
summarize_hp_nodes <- function(g, subset_type, subset_value) {
  
  node_name <- V(g)$name
  
  label <- str_remove(node_name, "^host_|^parasite_")
  
  node_type <- V(g)$node_type
  
  tibble(
    subset_type = subset_type,
    subset_value = subset_value,
    node = node_name,
    node_type = node_type,
    label = label,
    spp_code = if_else(
      node_type == "Host",
      label,
      NA_character_
    ),
    
    parasite_name = if_else(
      node_type == "Parasite",
      label,
      NA_character_
    ),
    degree = degree(g),
    betweenness = betweenness(g, normalized = TRUE),
    closeness = igraph::closeness(g, normalized = TRUE),
    eigen = eigen_centrality(g)$vector
  )
}

#pooled node centrality
g_meta <- build_hp_graph(hp_edges)

meta_node_summary <- summarize_hp_nodes(
  g_meta,
  "pooled",
  "all_years"
)

meta_node_summary %>%
  arrange(desc(eigen))

#year-specific node centrality
yearly_node_summary <- hp_edges %>%
  group_split(year) %>%
  map_dfr(function(df_year) {
    
    yr <- unique(df_year$year)
    
    g_year <- build_hp_graph(df_year)
    
    summarize_hp_nodes(
      g = g_year,
      subset_type = "year",
      subset_value = as.character(yr)
    )
  })

yearly_node_summary

#longevity-specific node centrality
longevity_node_summary <- hp_edges %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(longevity), longevity != "") %>%
  group_split(longevity) %>%
  map_dfr(function(df_longevity) {
    
    lon <- unique(df_longevity$longevity)
    
    g_lon <- build_hp_graph(df_longevity)
    
    summarize_hp_nodes(
      g = g_lon,
      subset_type = "longevity",
      subset_value = as.character(lon)
    )
  })

longevity_node_summary

#combined node summaries
node_summary <- bind_rows(
  meta_node_summary,
  yearly_node_summary,
  longevity_node_summary
)

node_summary


#most central hosts + parasites
top_hosts <- meta_node_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(node_type == "Host") %>%
  arrange(desc(degree))

top_hosts

  dplyr::filter(node_type == "Parasite") %>%
  arrange(desc(degree))

top_parasites

  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(label, degree), y = degree)) +
  geom_col() +

  labs(
    x = "Host species",
```

## 2.4 Stage 5.5 — Reusable subnetwork builder

**Status:** Core utility.

```{r stage-055-subnetwork-builder}
#stage 5.5: subnetwork builder

#filtering hp_edges
filter_hp_edges <- function(data,
                            years = NULL,
                            longevity_classes = NULL,
                            sites = NULL,
                            hosts = NULL,
                            parasites = NULL) {
  
  out <- data
  
  if (!is.null(years)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(year %in% years)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(longevity_classes)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(longevity %in% longevity_classes)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(sites)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(site_code %in% sites)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(hosts)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(spp_code %in% hosts)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(parasites)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(parasite_name %in% parasites)
  }
  
  out
}


#build edge list + graph from any filtered hp_edges table
make_hp_network <- function(data,
                            subset_type = "custom",
                            subset_value = "custom") {
  
  edge_df <- data %>%
    distinct(spp_code, parasite_name) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(spp_code),
      !is.na(parasite_name),
      spp_code != "",
      parasite_name != ""
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      from = paste0("host_", spp_code),
      to = paste0("parasite_", parasite_name),
      weight = 1
    ) %>%
    select(from, to, weight)
  
  node_df <- tibble(
    name = unique(c(edge_df$from, edge_df$to))
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      node_type = case_when(
        str_detect(name, "^host_") ~ "Host",
        str_detect(name, "^parasite_") ~ "Parasite",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      label = str_remove(name, "^host_|^parasite_"),
      bipartite_type = node_type == "Host"
    )
  
  g <- graph_from_data_frame(
    d = edge_df,
    vertices = node_df,
    directed = FALSE
  )
  
  list(
    graph = g,
    edges = edge_df,
    nodes = node_df,
    subset_type = subset_type,
    subset_value = subset_value
  )
}

#wrapped: filter + build network
build_subset_network <- function(data,
                                 years = NULL,
                                 longevity_classes = NULL,
                                 sites = NULL,
                                 hosts = NULL,
                                 parasites = NULL,
                                 subset_type = "custom",
                                 subset_value = "custom") {
  
  filtered_data <- filter_hp_edges(
    data = data,
    years = years,
    longevity_classes = longevity_classes,
    sites = sites,
    hosts = hosts,
    parasites = parasites
  )
  
  network <- make_hp_network(
    data = filtered_data,
    subset_type = subset_type,
    subset_value = subset_value
  )
  
  network$raw_data <- filtered_data
  
  network
}

#test
test_net <- build_subset_network(
  data = hp_edges,
  years = 2017,
  subset_type = "year",
  subset_value = "2017"
)

test_net$graph

summarize_hp_graph(
  g = test_net$graph,
  subset_type = test_net$subset_type,
  subset_value = test_net$subset_value
)
```

## 2.5 Retained descriptive interpretations

### Original written interpretations

- More even parasite importance distribution (9 with max degree 5).
- High-degree parasites are mostly trematodes (snail dependent?).
- High connectance/density plus low modularity.
- The same “big dog” amphibians recur, especially TATO and PSRE.
- Permanent ponds had the richest parasite communities, semi-permanent ponds had the densest interaction networks, and temporary ponds had the greatest modularity.
- Identify dominant parasites by year, dynamic host breadth, and imbalance among parasite importance.

### Earlier overall synthesis, retained as provisional

- The amphibian host–parasite community forms a highly connected, weakly modular network characterized by extensive parasite sharing among hosts.
- Network organization remained stable through time despite substantial annual variation in parasite richness and interaction number.
- Pond longevity influenced both parasite diversity and network architecture, with permanent ponds supporting the most diverse parasite communities.
- A small number of host species and parasites consistently occupied central positions within the network and likely contribute disproportionately to parasite transmission dynamics.
- Preliminary work suggested that bullfrog presence was associated with changes in host–parasite network structure, while Bd burden appeared to be driven more by host species than by pooled network centrality.

**Current status of these claims:** The first and fourth bullets remain useful descriptive summaries. The temporal-stability claim is too strong after the within-site turnover analysis. The longevity and bullfrog claims remain provisional until Stages 23–24 and a site-year modularity analysis pass diagnostics.

# 3. H1 and H2 — Shared ecological-driver workflow

H1 and H2 use the same site-year response models. Each coefficient answers a different hypothesis, so the analysis is organized jointly rather than duplicated.

## 3.1 Environmental covariate preparation

**Status:** Optional supporting. Required only when dynamic pond variables such as depth, area, trophic state, or drying are included. Longevity can be analyzed without these variables.

```{r h12-environmental-prep}
# --- site-level static properties (site_info) ---
env_site <- site_info %>%
  select(
    site_code,
    longevity,
    class,
    origin,
    elevation_m,
    property_area_m2,
    meta_comm_area_m2,
    latitude,
    longitude
  )

# STAGE 21: Match environmental conditions to sampling dates more
# precisely, and fix the arbitrary first(na.omit(trophic_state)) pick
# from Stage 11's env_site_year

# Safe mean: returns NA instead of NaN when every value is missing
safe_mean <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

# Safe mode: returns NA when every value is missing or blank
safe_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & x != ""]

  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  tab <- table(x)

  # Deterministic choice if multiple categories are tied
  sort(names(tab)[tab == max(tab)])[1]
}

wetland_info <- wetland_info %>%
  mutate(
    trophic_state = trophic_state %>%
      str_to_lower() %>%
      str_trim(),

    dry_clean = dry %>%
      as.character() %>%
      str_to_upper() %>%
      str_trim(),

    dry_logical = case_when(
      dry_clean %in% c("TRUE", "T", "1", "Y", "YES")  ~ TRUE,
      dry_clean %in% c("FALSE", "F", "0", "N", "NO") ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA
    )
  )

env_site_year <- wetland_info %>%
  rename(site_code = site) %>%
  group_by(site_code, year) %>%
  summarize(
    pond_area_m = safe_mean(pond_area_m),
    perimeter_m = safe_mean(perimeter_m),
    max_depth_m = safe_mean(max_depth_m),

    trophic_state = safe_mode(trophic_state),

    frac_dry = safe_mean(as.numeric(dry_logical)),

    n_assessments = n(),
    n_dry_assessments = sum(!is.na(dry_logical)),
    n_trophic_assessments = sum(!is.na(trophic_state)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ever_dry = case_when(
      is.na(frac_dry) ~ NA,
      frac_dry > 0 ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  )

env_site_year
```

## 3.2 Stage 13 — Independent bullfrog detection

**Status:** Core. This supersedes Stage 6. `bullfrog_detected` is based on `survey_spp` and `visual_spp`; unsurveyed site-years remain missing rather than being forced to absence.

```{r h12-stage-13-bullfrog-surveys}
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)



# STAGE 13: Define bullfrog presence independently of parasite/Bd sampling
# Stage 6's bullfrog_present was derived from hp_edges; site-year
# was called "bullfrog absent" whenever RACA didn't show up in the
# dissection-based interaction table. That conflates "not dissected" with
# "biologically absent." Rebuilding bullfrog status from the independent
# netting (survey_spp) and visual-encounter (visual_spp) surveys instead,
# and leaving status as NA for site-years that were never surveyed for
# amphibians at all - this supersedes hp_edges_bf from Stage 6 for any
# confirmatory analysis.

bullfrog_survey_status <- bind_rows(

  survey_spp %>%
    transmute(
      site_code,
      year,
      survey_id = survey_code,
      detected = spp_code == "RACA",
      source = "survey_spp"
    ),

  visual_spp %>%
    transmute(
      site_code = site,
      year = as.integer(str_sub(as.character(code), 1, 4)),
      survey_id = visual_code,
      detected = spp_code == "RACA",
      source = "visual_spp"
    )

) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(year)
  ) %>%
  group_by(site_code, year) %>%
  summarize(
    bullfrog_detected = any(detected),
    n_surveys = n_distinct(survey_id),
    survey_sources = paste(sort(unique(source)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bullfrog_survey_status %>%
  count(bullfrog_detected)

# how many site-years in the network data have NO independent survey
# coverage at all? these should stay NA, not get forced to FALSE
hp_edges %>%
  distinct(site_code, year) %>%
  left_join(bullfrog_survey_status, by = c("site_code", "year")) %>%
  summarize(
    n_site_years = n(),
    n_unsurveyed = sum(is.na(bullfrog_detected))
  )

# rebuilt bullfrog-tagged edge table using survey-based status
hp_edges_bf2 <- hp_edges %>%
  left_join(bullfrog_survey_status, by = c("site_code", "year"))

hp_edges_bf2 %>%
  count(bullfrog_detected, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 3.3 Stage 14 — Check bullfrog–permanence overlap and estimability

**Status:** Core. This is primarily a support/overlap check, not proof that the predictors are unconfounded. Sparse or absent combinations determine whether an interaction can be estimated.

```{r h12-stage-14-overlap}
# STAGE 14: Test whether bullfrog detection and pond longevity are confounded

analysis_df <- site_year_network_summary %>%
  select(-any_of(c("bullfrog_present", "bullfrog_detected"))) %>%
  left_join(bullfrog_survey_status, by = c("site_code", "year")) %>%
  left_join(env_site_year, by = c("site_code", "year"))

# Site-year support
analysis_df %>%
  count(longevity, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_by(longevity) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))

# Distinct-site support
analysis_df %>%
  distinct(site_code, longevity, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  count(longevity, bullfrog_detected)

# Does habitat predict bullfrog detection?
m_bullfrog_habitat <- glmmTMB(
  bullfrog_detected ~
    longevity +
    scale(log1p(pond_area_m)) +
    scale(max_depth_m) +
    ever_dry +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = binomial,
  data = analysis_df
)

summary(m_bullfrog_habitat)

# Check origin/class as a more direct anthropogenic-disturbance proxy
# than longevity alone.
site_info %>%
  count(class, origin, longevity)

# flag sparse cells directly rather than eyeballing the proportions table
driver_support <- analysis_df %>%
  count(longevity, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_by(longevity) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))

driver_support %>% filter(n < 5)

# distinct-pond version - a proportion built on the same 2 ponds resurveyed
# across years isn't real replication, even if the site-year count is high
pond_support <- analysis_df %>%
  distinct(site_code, longevity, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  count(longevity, bullfrog_detected)

pond_support %>% filter(n < 3)

# fallback if the 3-way split is too sparse: collapse to permanent vs.
# non-permanent. Uses string matching so it doesn't depend on the exact
# level spelling/capitalization in site_info
analysis_df <- analysis_df %>%
  mutate(
    longevity_binary = if_else(
      str_detect(str_to_lower(longevity), "perm") &
        !str_detect(str_to_lower(longevity), "semi"),
      "permanent",
      "non-permanent"
    )
  )

analysis_df %>%
  count(longevity_binary, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_by(longevity_binary) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n))
```

### Retained interpretation

- No significant environmental predictors of bullfrog detection besides year.


## 3.4 Stage 15 — Quantify network sampling effort

**Status:** Core. This stage defines the observation process shared by H1 and H2 and supports sensitivity analyses for H3.

```{r h12-stage-15-effort}
# STAGE 15: Quantify + control network sampling effort (arxiv de aguiar)
network_effort <- amphib_dissect %>%
  filter(dissected %in% TRUE) %>%
  group_by(site_code, year) %>%
  summarize(
    total_dissected = n(),
    host_species_dissected = n_distinct(spp_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

network_effort

network_df <- analysis_df %>%
  left_join(network_effort, by = c("site_code", "year"))

network_df %>%
  summarize(
    n_missing_effort = sum(is.na(total_dissected)),
    min_dissected = min(total_dissected, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_dissected = max(total_dissected, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# threshold sensitivity - does the bullfrog/longevity signal hold across
# minimum-effort cutoffs, rather than resting on one arbitrary threshold?
effort_sensitivity <- map_dfr(
  c(5, 10, 20, 30),
  function(threshold) {
    network_df %>%
      filter(total_dissected >= threshold) %>%
      mutate(minimum_effort = threshold)
  }
)

effort_sensitivity %>%
  count(minimum_effort)

# flag (don't silently drop) unstable/near-degenerate networks
network_df <- network_df %>%
  mutate(
    network_too_small = n_hosts < 2 | n_parasites < 3
  )

network_df %>%
  count(network_too_small)
```

## 3.5 Stage 22 — Shared model-diagnostic helper

**Status:** Core utility. The corrected helper is retained once; the duplicated earlier copy is not repeated.

```{r shared-stage-22-diagnostics}

# STAGE 22: Formal model diagnostics, collinearity, and complete-case
# reporting for the GLMMs above

library(DHARMa)
library(tidyverse)

check_model <- function(
    model,
    model_name,
    model_data = NULL,
    time_var = NULL,
    group_var = NULL,
    min_time_points = 4
) {

  res <- simulateResiduals(
    fittedModel = model,
    n = 1000
  )

  cat("\n---", model_name, "---\n")

  plot(res)

  dispersion_test <- testDispersion(
    res,
    plot = FALSE
  )

  zero_test <- testZeroInflation(
    res,
    plot = FALSE
  )

  uniformity_test <- testUniformity(
    res,
    plot = FALSE
  )

  print(uniformity_test)
  print(dispersion_test)
  print(zero_test)

  temporal_overall <- NULL
  temporal_by_group <- NULL

  if (!is.null(time_var) && !is.null(group_var)) {

    if (length(time_var) != length(res$scaledResiduals) ||
        length(group_var) != length(res$scaledResiduals)) {
      stop(
        "time_var and group_var must correspond exactly to the rows ",
        "used to fit the model."
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Overall temporal test
    # Aggregate residuals across sites within each year
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    complete_temporal <- !is.na(time_var) & !is.na(group_var)

    res_temporal <- recalculateResiduals(
      res,
      sel = complete_temporal
    )

    time_complete <- time_var[complete_temporal]

    year_factor <- factor(
      time_complete,
      levels = sort(unique(time_complete))
    )

    res_by_year <- recalculateResiduals(
      res_temporal,
      group = year_factor
    )

    temporal_overall <- testTemporalAutocorrelation(
      res_by_year,
      time = sort(unique(time_complete)),
      plot = TRUE
    )

    cat("\nOverall temporal autocorrelation:\n")
    print(temporal_overall)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Within-site temporal tests
    # Requires one observation per site-year
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    temporal_df <- tibble(
      row_id = seq_along(time_var),
      time = time_var,
      group = as.character(group_var)
    ) %>%
      filter(
        !is.na(time),
        !is.na(group)
      )

    repeated_site_years <- temporal_df %>%
      count(group, time) %>%
      filter(n > 1)

    if (nrow(repeated_site_years) > 0) {

      warning(
        "Some groups contain multiple observations in the same year. ",
        "The within-group temporal tests were skipped. Aggregate to one ",
        "observation per group-year first."
      )

    } else {

      temporal_by_group <- temporal_df %>%
        group_split(group) %>%
        map_dfr(function(df_group) {

          df_group <- df_group %>%
            arrange(time)

          group_name <- first(df_group$group)

          if (nrow(df_group) < min_time_points) {
            return(
              tibble(
                group = group_name,
                n_years = nrow(df_group),
                statistic = NA_real_,
                p_value = NA_real_
              )
            )
          }

          keep_rows <- seq_along(time_var) %in% df_group$row_id

          res_group <- recalculateResiduals(
            res,
            sel = keep_rows
          )

          autocorrelation_test <- testTemporalAutocorrelation(
            res_group,
            time = df_group$time,
            plot = FALSE
          )

          tibble(
            group = group_name,
            n_years = nrow(df_group),
            statistic = unname(
              autocorrelation_test$statistic
            ),
            p_value = autocorrelation_test$p.value
          )
        }) %>%
        mutate(
          p_adjusted = p.adjust(
            p_value,
            method = "BH"
          )
        )

      cat("\nWithin-site temporal autocorrelation tests:\n")
      print(temporal_by_group)
    }
  }

  invisible(
    list(
      residuals = res,
      uniformity = uniformity_test,
      dispersion = dispersion_test,
      zero_inflation = zero_test,
      temporal_overall = temporal_overall,
      temporal_by_group = temporal_by_group
    )
  )
}
```

## 3.6 Stage 23 — Rebuild parasite richness from the sampling frame

**Status:** Core, unresolved.

This replaces the Stage 16 richness dataset, which was filtered to networks with at least three parasite taxa. The final model must start from all adequately sampled site-years. Before assigning zero richness, confirm that the absence of a parasite record means examination was completed and no parasites were found rather than that parasite records are missing.

```{r h12-stage-23-richness}
# STAGE 23: Rebuild the parasite-richness dataset correctly
#
# The stuck attempt above (and Stage 16's m_richness) built richness_model_df
# from network_df_model, which is filtered to !network_too_small - i.e.
# n_parasites >= 3 by construction. That's why richness could never go
# below 3: the model was fit on data where low richness was already
# excluded. Rebuilding from the dissection records directly instead, so
# 0/1/2-richness site-years are actually in the model.

parasite_richness_observed <- hp_edges %>%
  distinct(site_code, year, parasite_name) %>%
  count(site_code, year, name = "n_parasites_observed")

richness_df <- network_effort %>%
  left_join(parasite_richness_observed, by = c("site_code", "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    # zero is a legitimate observation here - network_effort only contains
    # site-years where dissection actually happened, so a site-year with
    # no match in parasite_richness_observed means examination was
    # completed and no parasites were found, not "not looked"
    n_parasites = replace_na(n_parasites_observed, 0)
  ) %>%
  select(-n_parasites_observed) %>%
  left_join(bullfrog_survey_status, by = c("site_code", "year")) %>%
  left_join(site_info %>% select(site_code, longevity), by = "site_code") %>%
  filter(!is.na(bullfrog_detected))

# verify the zero-richness assumption before trusting it: does
# amphib_parasite ever contain an explicit negative record (checked for a
# parasite, none found), or are only positive detections ever entered?
amphib_parasite %>%
  summarize(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_zero_count = sum(parasite_cnt == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_presence_false = sum(presence %in% c(FALSE, "N", "No", "NO", 0), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# how many dissected individuals have NO row at all in amphib_parasite -
# richness_df currently treats every one of these as a confirmed zero
amphib_dissect %>%
  distinct(dissect_code) %>%
  anti_join(amphib_parasite %>% distinct(dissect_code), by = "dissect_code") %>%
  nrow()

richness_df %>%
  summarize(
    n_site_years = n(),
    min_richness = min(n_parasites),
    max_richness = max(n_parasites),
    n_zero = sum(n_parasites == 0),
    n_one  = sum(n_parasites == 1),
    n_two  = sum(n_parasites == 2)
  )

# additive per Stage 15.5's estimability check - not bullfrog_detected * longevity
m_richness_poisson <- glmmTMB(
  n_parasites ~
    bullfrog_detected +
    longevity +
    scale(year) +
    scale(log1p(total_dissected)) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = poisson,
  data = richness_df,
  na.action = na.fail
)

summary(m_richness_poisson)

res_richness_poisson <- simulateResiduals(m_richness_poisson, n = 1000)
plot(res_richness_poisson)
testUniformity(res_richness_poisson)
testDispersion(res_richness_poisson)
testZeroInflation(res_richness_poisson)

# escalate to COM-Poisson if the Poisson model is underdispersed (a
# dispersion ratio < 1 with a significant test above) - nbinom2 only
# corrects overdispersion, so it's the wrong escalation for this case
m_richness_compois <- update(m_richness_poisson, family = compois)

res_richness_compois <- simulateResiduals(m_richness_compois, n = 1000)
plot(res_richness_compois)
testUniformity(res_richness_compois)
testDispersion(res_richness_compois)
testZeroInflation(res_richness_compois)

summary(m_richness_compois)

# done when either:
# (a) one of the two models above has acceptable DHARMa diagnostics - use
#     it and interpret those coefficients, or
# (b) neither does - write down that richness cannot currently support a
#     reliable model instead of reporting a coefficient anyway
```

### Decision rule for the richness result

- Use the Poisson model only if DHARMa diagnostics are acceptable.
- Escalate to COM-Poisson for genuine underdispersion.
- If neither model fits adequately, report that parasite richness cannot currently support reliable inference rather than interpreting an unstable coefficient.

## 3.7 Stage 24 — Validate the connectance model

**Status:** Core, unresolved. This is currently the most promising H1/H2 inferential outcome.

```{r h12-stage-24-connectance}
# STAGE 24: Validate the connectance model
#
# Connectance was more promising than richness in Stage 16 and could
# become the main H1/H2 result - so it gets the full diagnostic
# treatment before that claim is trusted.

connectance_df <- network_df %>%
  filter(
    !network_too_small,
    !is.na(bullfrog_detected),
    !is.na(longevity),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(total_dissected),
    !is.na(site_code)
  ) %>%
  mutate(possible_links = n_hosts * n_parasites)

nrow(network_df)
nrow(connectance_df)

# additive per Stage 15.5 - no interaction unless the estimability check
# there actually supports one
m_connectance_validated <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(n_edges, possible_links - n_edges) ~
    bullfrog_detected +
    longevity +
    scale(year) +
    scale(log1p(total_dissected)) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = betabinomial,
  data = connectance_df,
  na.action = na.fail
)

summary(m_connectance_validated)

# convergence + positive-definite Hessian
diagnose(m_connectance_validated)
m_connectance_validated$sdr$pdHess

# DHARMa uniformity, dispersion, zero-inflation, residual-vs-predicted
check_model(
  m_connectance_validated,
  "connectance (validated, additive)",
  model_data = connectance_df,
  time_var = connectance_df$year,
  group_var = connectance_df$site_code
)

# collinearity - is bullfrog_detected confounded with longevity or effort
# in this exact complete-case dataset (may differ slightly from Stage 15.5's
# driver_df due to the na.omit above)
connectance_df %>%
  count(longevity, bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_by(longevity) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

connectance_df %>%
  summarize(cor_year_effort = cor(year, log1p(total_dissected), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))

# sensitivity to minimum dissection threshold - does the bullfrog_detected
# coefficient keep its sign as weakly-sampled site-years are dropped?
connectance_sensitivity <- map_dfr(
  c(5, 10, 20, 30),
  function(threshold) {

    df_thresh <- connectance_df %>%
      filter(total_dissected >= threshold)

    if (n_distinct(df_thresh$bullfrog_detected) < 2 || nrow(df_thresh) < 10) {
      return(tibble(minimum_effort = threshold, n = nrow(df_thresh), bullfrog_coef = NA_real_))
    }

    m_thresh <- glmmTMB(
      cbind(n_edges, possible_links - n_edges) ~
        bullfrog_detected + longevity + scale(year) + scale(log1p(total_dissected)) +
        (1 | site_code),
      family = betabinomial,
      data = df_thresh
    )

    tibble(
      minimum_effort = threshold,
      n = nrow(df_thresh),
      bullfrog_coef = fixef(m_thresh)$cond[["bullfrog_detectedTRUE"]]
    )
  }
)

connectance_sensitivity
```

## 3.8 Stage 17 — Bipartite modularity and null comparison

**Status:** Needs revision.

This replaces Louvain modularity for final biological interpretation. The current pooled bullfrog comparison asks whether each pooled network is unusual relative to its own fixed-margin null model; it does **not** by itself test whether bullfrog-detected and nondetected site-years differ significantly. A replicated site-year modularity or null-standardized modularity model is still needed.

```{r h12-stage-17-modularity}
# STAGE 17: Recalculate modularity using a bipartite-specific method + null model
library(bipartite)

compute_bipartite_modularity <- function(edges_df) {

  web <- edges_df %>%
    distinct(spp_code, parasite_name) %>%
    mutate(value = 1L) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = parasite_name,
      values_from = value,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("spp_code") %>%
    as.matrix()

  observed_modularity <- bipartite::networklevel(
    web,
    index = "modularity",
    weighted = FALSE
  )

  null_webs <- vegan::permatswap(
    web,
    method = "quasiswap",
    fixedmar = "both",
    mtype = "prab",
    times = 999
  )$perm

  null_modularity <- map_dbl(
    null_webs,
    ~ bipartite::networklevel(.x, index = "modularity", weighted = FALSE)
  )

  tibble(
    observed_modularity = observed_modularity,
    null_mean = mean(null_modularity),
    null_sd = sd(null_modularity),
    modularity_z = (observed_modularity - mean(null_modularity)) / sd(null_modularity)
  )
}

# sanity check against the full metaweb's Louvain modularity from Stage 3-4
metaweb_modularity <- compute_bipartite_modularity(hp_edges)
metaweb_modularity

# bullfrog present/absent subsets - replaces Stage 6/9's Louvain-based
# modularity comparison
bipartite_modularity_by_bullfrog <- hp_edges_bf2 %>%
  filter(!is.na(bullfrog_detected)) %>%
  group_by(bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_modify(~ compute_bipartite_modularity(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

bipartite_modularity_by_bullfrog
```

### Retained interpretation

- Original note: “bullfrog presence → significant modularity difference vs null model.”

**Current status:** Revise this claim. The result may show that one or both pooled networks differ from their null expectations, but a direct between-status test is still required.

| Outcome | Current evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Parasite richness | Earlier models suggested higher richness with bullfrogs and some longevity differences | Not interpretable until Stage 23 is resolved |
| Connectance | Earlier models suggested lower connectance with bullfrogs and longevity differences | Provisional pending Stage 24 diagnostics and sensitivity checks |
| Modularity | Pooled bipartite null comparisons suggest structural differences | Needs replicated site-year analysis |
| Bullfrog × longevity interaction | Earlier first-pass model suggested an interaction in some cells | Do not retain unless overlap/support is adequate |

- Semi-permanence and its interaction with bullfrog presence were significant for connectance.

These statements belong to the superseded Stage 16 model and must not be treated as final results.

# 4. H3 — Temporal network dynamics

## 4.1 Descriptive annual dynamics from Stages 4–5

The annual link count, connectance, modularity, and node trajectories above provide descriptive context. Similar aggregate metrics across years do not imply that the same taxa or interactions persisted.

## 4.2 Stage 10 — Host projection and Jaccard similarity

**Status:** Supporting/descriptive. This describes shared parasite assemblages among hosts and motivated the formal beta-diversity analysis. It is not itself a transmission model.

```{r h3-stage-10-host-projection}
#stage 10

build_host_jaccard_projection <- function(edge_df) {
  
  # Binary host x parasite incidence matrix
  incidence <- edge_df %>%
    distinct(spp_code, parasite_name) %>%
    mutate(present = 1L) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = parasite_name,
      values_from = present,
      values_fill = 0
    )
  
  host_names <- incidence$spp_code
  
  host_matrix <- incidence %>%
    select(-spp_code) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  rownames(host_matrix) <- host_names
  
  # Jaccard similarity:
  # shared parasites / total unique parasites across the pair
  jaccard_matrix <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = nrow(host_matrix),
    ncol = nrow(host_matrix),
    dimnames = list(host_names, host_names)
  )
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(host_matrix))) {
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(host_matrix))) {
      
      host_i <- host_matrix[i, ] > 0
      host_j <- host_matrix[j, ] > 0
      
      intersection <- sum(host_i & host_j)
      union <- sum(host_i | host_j)
      
      jaccard_matrix[i, j] <- ifelse(
        union == 0,
        NA_real_,
        intersection / union
      )
    }
  }
  
  diag(jaccard_matrix) <- 0
  
  # Convert upper triangle to edge table
  projection_edges <- as.data.frame(as.table(jaccard_matrix)) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    rename(
      from = Var1,
      to = Var2,
      jaccard = Freq
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      from = as.character(from),
      to = as.character(to)
    ) %>%
    filter(
      from < to,
      !is.na(jaccard),
      jaccard > 0
    )
  
  projection_nodes <- tibble(
    name = host_names,
    parasite_richness = rowSums(host_matrix > 0)
  )
  
  g_projection <- graph_from_data_frame(
    d = projection_edges,
    vertices = projection_nodes,
    directed = FALSE
  )
  
  list(
    graph = g_projection,
    edges = projection_edges,
    nodes = projection_nodes,
    incidence_matrix = host_matrix,
    jaccard_matrix = jaccard_matrix
  )
}
```

## 4.3 Stage 13 — Pooled/shared-site temporal beta diversity

**Status:** Supporting sensitivity analysis. This analysis correctly partitions total interaction dissimilarity into rewiring among shared taxa (`beta_os`) and the interaction-level contribution associated with turnover (`beta_st`). Pooled networks can still mix spatial and temporal change.

```{r h3-stage-13-pooled-beta}
# STAGE 13: Temporal network dissimilarity
# Rewiring vs. species-turnover contributions

# 1. Clean binary interaction table

hp_edges_beta <- hp_edges |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    site_code = as.character(site_code),
    year = as.integer(year),
    host = as.character(spp_code),
    parasite = as.character(parasite_name)
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(host),
    !is.na(parasite),
    host != "",
    parasite != ""
  ) |>
  dplyr::distinct(site_code, year, host, parasite)



# 2. Convert an edge table to a binary incidence matrix


edges_to_matrix <- function(edges, hosts, parasites) {

  web <- matrix(
    0L,
    nrow = length(hosts),
    ncol = length(parasites),
    dimnames = list(hosts, parasites)
  )

  if (nrow(edges) > 0) {

    row_id <- match(edges$host, hosts)
    col_id <- match(edges$parasite, parasites)

    web[cbind(row_id, col_id)] <- 1L
  }

  web
}



# 3. Compare two networks
#
# βS  = taxonomic composition dissimilarity
# βWN = total interaction-network dissimilarity
# βOS = contribution from rewiring among shared taxa
# βST = contribution from taxa not shared between networks
#
# Under partitioning = "commondenom":
# βWN = βOS + βST


network_beta <- function(edges_a, edges_b) {

  edges_a <- edges_a |>
    dplyr::distinct(host, parasite)

  edges_b <- edges_b |>
    dplyr::distinct(host, parasite)

  # Return missing results if either network has no interactions
  if (nrow(edges_a) == 0 || nrow(edges_b) == 0) {

    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        beta_s = NA_real_,
        beta_os = NA_real_,
        beta_st = NA_real_,
        beta_wn = NA_real_,
        rewiring_fraction = NA_real_,
        turnover_fraction = NA_real_,
        decomposition_error = NA_real_,
        n_hosts_a = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_a$host),
        n_hosts_b = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_b$host),
        n_shared_hosts = length(
          intersect(unique(edges_a$host), unique(edges_b$host))
        ),
        n_parasites_a = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_a$parasite),
        n_parasites_b = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_b$parasite),
        n_shared_parasites = length(
          intersect(unique(edges_a$parasite), unique(edges_b$parasite))
        ),
        n_links_a = nrow(edges_a),
        n_links_b = nrow(edges_b),
        n_shared_links = 0L
      )
    )
  }

  # Use the same matrix dimensions for both networks
  all_hosts <- sort(
    union(unique(edges_a$host), unique(edges_b$host))
  )

  all_parasites <- sort(
    union(unique(edges_a$parasite), unique(edges_b$parasite))
  )

  web_a <- edges_to_matrix(
    edges = edges_a,
    hosts = all_hosts,
    parasites = all_parasites
  )

  web_b <- edges_to_matrix(
    edges = edges_b,
    hosts = all_hosts,
    parasites = all_parasites
  )

  web_array <- array(
    0L,
    dim = c(
      length(all_hosts),
      length(all_parasites),
      2
    ),
    dimnames = list(
      host = all_hosts,
      parasite = all_parasites,
      network = c("A", "B")
    )
  )

  web_array[, , "A"] <- web_a
  web_array[, , "B"] <- web_b

  beta <- bipartite::betalinkr(
    webarray = web_array,
    index = "jaccard",
    binary = TRUE,
    partitioning = "commondenom",
    proportions = FALSE,
    distofempty = "zero"
  )

  beta_s <- unname(beta["S"])
  beta_os <- unname(beta["OS"])
  beta_st <- unname(beta["ST"])
  beta_wn <- unname(beta["WN"])

  links_a <- paste(edges_a$host, edges_a$parasite, sep = "__")
  links_b <- paste(edges_b$host, edges_b$parasite, sep = "__")

  tibble::tibble(
    # Taxonomic dissimilarity; informative but not an additive component
    beta_s = beta_s,

    # Additive interaction-network components
    beta_os = beta_os,
    beta_st = beta_st,
    beta_wn = beta_wn,

    # Relative contribution to total network dissimilarity
    rewiring_fraction = dplyr::if_else(
      beta_wn > 0,
      beta_os / beta_wn,
      NA_real_
    ),

    turnover_fraction = dplyr::if_else(
      beta_wn > 0,
      beta_st / beta_wn,
      NA_real_
    ),

    # Should be approximately zero
    decomposition_error = beta_wn - beta_os - beta_st,

    # Diagnostic information
    n_hosts_a = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_a$host),
    n_hosts_b = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_b$host),

    n_shared_hosts = length(
      intersect(unique(edges_a$host), unique(edges_b$host))
    ),

    n_parasites_a = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_a$parasite),
    n_parasites_b = dplyr::n_distinct(edges_b$parasite),

    n_shared_parasites = length(
      intersect(
        unique(edges_a$parasite),
        unique(edges_b$parasite)
      )
    ),

    n_links_a = nrow(edges_a),
    n_links_b = nrow(edges_b),

    n_shared_links = length(
      intersect(links_a, links_b)
    )
  )
}



# 4. Compare a pair of years
#
# shared_sites_only = TRUE prevents changing site composition
# from being counted as temporal network change.


compare_year_pair <- function(
    edge_data,
    year_from,
    year_to,
    shared_sites_only = TRUE
) {

  edges_from_raw <- edge_data |>
    dplyr::filter(year == year_from)

  edges_to_raw <- edge_data |>
    dplyr::filter(year == year_to)

  sites_from <- unique(edges_from_raw$site_code)
  sites_to <- unique(edges_to_raw$site_code)
  shared_sites <- intersect(sites_from, sites_to)

  if (shared_sites_only) {

    edges_from <- edges_from_raw |>
      dplyr::filter(site_code %in% shared_sites)

    edges_to <- edges_to_raw |>
      dplyr::filter(site_code %in% shared_sites)

  } else {

    edges_from <- edges_from_raw
    edges_to <- edges_to_raw
  }

  network_beta(edges_from, edges_to) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      year_from = year_from,
      year_to = year_to,
      year_gap = year_to - year_from,
      is_adjacent_year = year_gap == 1,
      comparison = paste(year_from, year_to, sep = "\u2013"),
      shared_sites_only = shared_sites_only,
      n_sites_from = length(sites_from),
      n_sites_to = length(sites_to),
      n_shared_sites = length(shared_sites),
      .before = 1
    )
}

# 8. Compare each pond with itself across adjacent years

site_level_rewiring <- purrr::map2_dfr(
  observed_year_transitions$year_from,
  observed_year_transitions$year_to,
  function(yr1, yr2) {

    gap <- yr2 - yr1

    sites_1 <- hp_edges_beta |>
      dplyr::filter(year == yr1) |>
      dplyr::distinct(site_code) |>
      dplyr::pull(site_code)

    sites_2 <- hp_edges_beta |>
      dplyr::filter(year == yr2) |>
      dplyr::distinct(site_code) |>
      dplyr::pull(site_code)

    shared_sites <- intersect(sites_1, sites_2)

    purrr::map_dfr(
      shared_sites,
      function(site_i) {

        edges_1 <- hp_edges_beta |>
          dplyr::filter(
            site_code == site_i,
            year == yr1
          )

        edges_2 <- hp_edges_beta |>
          dplyr::filter(
            site_code == site_i,
            year == yr2
          )

        network_beta(edges_1, edges_2) |>
          dplyr::mutate(
            site_code = site_i,
            year_from = yr1,
            year_to = yr2,
            year_gap = gap,
            is_adjacent_year = gap == 1,
            .before = 1
          )
      }
    )
  }
)

site_level_rewiring

site_level_rewiring <- site_level_rewiring |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    adequate_network_size =
      n_links_a >= minimum_links &
      n_links_b >= minimum_links

  dplyr::group_by(year_from, year_to) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_sites = dplyr::n(),

    mean_beta_wn = mean(beta_wn),
    mean_beta_os = mean(beta_os),
    mean_beta_st = mean(beta_st),

    median_beta_wn = median(beta_wn),
    median_beta_os = median(beta_os),

    mean_rewiring_fraction =
      mean(rewiring_fraction, na.rm = TRUE),

```

### Retained interpretation from the pooled analysis

- Network composition was temporally dynamic even when comparisons were limited to the same ponds.
- Interaction rewiring appeared to be a major component of temporal network variation.

**Current status:** The second claim is superseded as the main conclusion by Stage 20. It remains useful as evidence that spatial aggregation changes the apparent decomposition.

## 4.4 Stage 20 — Within-site turnover versus rewiring

**Status:** Core. This is the primary H3 analysis because each pond is compared with itself across adjacent years. The bootstrap must compare `beta_os` with `beta_st`, not raw taxonomic dissimilarity `beta_s`.

```{r h3-stage-20-within-site}
# STAGE 20: Strengthen the rewiring decomposition from stage 12

# within-site, year-to-year comparisons only - pooling all sites can make
# species turnover look like rewiring

within_site_rewiring <- hp_edges %>%
  transmute(
    site_code,
    year = as.integer(year),
    host = as.character(spp_code),
    parasite = as.character(parasite_name)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(host),
    !is.na(parasite)
  ) %>%
  distinct(site_code, year, host, parasite) %>%
  group_by(site_code) %>%
  group_modify(function(df_site, keys) {

    yrs <- sort(unique(df_site$year))

    if (length(yrs) < 2) {
      return(tibble())
    }

    map_dfr(
      seq_len(length(yrs) - 1),
      function(i) {

        yr1 <- yrs[i]
        yr2 <- yrs[i + 1]

        # Compare only adjacent calendar years
        if (yr2 - yr1 != 1) {
          return(tibble())
        }

        e1 <- df_site %>%
          filter(year == yr1) %>%
          select(host, parasite)

        e2 <- df_site %>%
          filter(year == yr2) %>%
          select(host, parasite)

        shared_hosts <- intersect(
          unique(e1$host),
          unique(e2$host)
        )

        shared_parasites <- intersect(
          unique(e1$parasite),
          unique(e2$parasite)
        )

        # Minimum requirements for estimating rewiring
        if (
          nrow(e1) < 3 ||
          nrow(e2) < 3 ||
          length(shared_hosts) < 2 ||
          length(shared_parasites) < 2
        ) {
          return(tibble())
        }

        network_beta(e1, e2) %>%
          mutate(
            year_from = yr1,
            year_to = yr2,
            year_gap = yr2 - yr1,
            n_shared_hosts_check = length(shared_hosts),
            n_shared_parasites_check = length(shared_parasites),
            .before = 1
          )
      }
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

within_site_rewiring

# bootstrap CIs for the annual rewiring fraction (beta_os), resampling
# sites with replacement
set.seed(6262026)

boot_rewiring <- map_dfr(
  1:1000,
  function(b) {

    boot_sites <- sample(
      unique(within_site_rewiring$site_code),
      replace = TRUE
    )

    boot_df <- map_dfr(boot_sites, function(s) {
      within_site_rewiring %>% filter(site_code == s)
    })

    boot_df %>%
      group_by(year_to) %>%
      summarize(
        mean_beta_os = mean(beta_os, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_beta_st = mean(beta_st, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(boot_id = b)
  }
)

rewiring_ci <- boot_rewiring %>%
  group_by(year_to) %>%
  summarize(
    beta_os_mean  = mean(mean_beta_os, na.rm = TRUE),
    beta_os_lower = quantile(mean_beta_os, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    beta_os_upper = quantile(mean_beta_os, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    beta_st_mean   = mean(mean_beta_st, na.rm = TRUE),
    beta_st_lower  = quantile(mean_beta_st, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    beta_st_upper  = quantile(mean_beta_st, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rewiring_ci

ggplot(rewiring_ci, aes(x = year_to)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = beta_os_lower, ymax = beta_os_upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = beta_os_mean), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = beta_st_lower, ymax = beta_st_upper), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkorange") +
  geom_line(aes(y = beta_st_mean), color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Dissimilarity (bootstrapped mean +/- 95% CI)",
    title = "Within-site rewiring (blue) vs. species turnover (orange), bootstrapped over sites"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# RACA first-detection event study - compares network change before/after
# first bullfrog detection at invaded ponds, with never-detected ponds as
# a comparison group, instead of pooling all bullfrog-present site-years
raca_first_detection <- bullfrog_survey_status %>%
  filter(bullfrog_detected) %>%
  group_by(site_code) %>%
  summarize(first_raca_year = min(year), .groups = "drop")

event_study_df <- site_year_network_summary %>%
  left_join(raca_first_detection, by = "site_code") %>%
  mutate(
    event_time = year - first_raca_year,
    ever_invaded = !is.na(first_raca_year)
  )

event_study_df

event_study_df %>%
  filter(ever_invaded, !is.na(event_time), abs(event_time) <= 5) %>%
  group_by(event_time) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_connectance = mean(connectance, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = event_time, y = mean_connectance)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  labs(
    x = "Years relative to first bullfrog detection",
    y = "Mean connectance",
    size = "n site-years",
    title = "Connectance before/after first bullfrog detection, invaded ponds"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Current interpretation

- Within the same pond across years, the species-turnover contribution was substantially larger than the rewiring contribution, approximately threefold in the preliminary summary.
- Change may therefore arise mainly from hosts or parasites entering or leaving the observed network rather than persistent taxa changing partners.
- The rewiring signal became smaller when ponds were compared with themselves, showing that pooled analyses can inflate apparent rewiring.
- The first-detection connectance plot showed a spike near event time zero but did not corroborate a simple post-detection decline; it remains exploratory because first detection is not the same as colonization.

### H3 claim currently supported

> Within-pond annual network change appears to be driven more by the turnover of observed taxa than by interaction rewiring among taxa shared between years, although unequal detection and sampling effort remain alternative explanations.

## 4.5 Planned H3 extensions

**Status:** Future work; no completed result yet.

- Partition networks by host life stage after checking stage-specific sampling and whether reproduction changes the observed composition.
- Compare drought and nondrought years using a clearly defined external drought classification.
- Examine seasonal differences in dominant hosts and parasites only if sampling dates provide enough repeated seasonal coverage.
- Repeat the within-site decomposition across dissection-effort thresholds or individual-level standardization.

```{r}
stages_to_compare <- c(
  "ADULT",
  "LARVA",
  "META"
)

# Retain only stages that actually occur in the data
stages_available <- intersect(
  stages_to_compare,
  unique(stage_edges$life_stage)
)

stage_pairs <- utils::combn(
  stages_available,
  2,
  simplify = FALSE
)

stage_beta_pairwise <- purrr::map_dfr(
  stage_pairs,
  function(stage_pair) {

    stage_a <- stage_pair[1]
    stage_b <- stage_pair[2]

    edges_a <- stage_edges |>
      dplyr::filter(life_stage == stage_a) |>
      dplyr::select(host, parasite)

    edges_b <- stage_edges |>
      dplyr::filter(life_stage == stage_b) |>
      dplyr::select(host, parasite)

    network_beta(
      edges_a = edges_a,
      edges_b = edges_b
    ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        stage_a = stage_a,
        stage_b = stage_b,
        comparison = paste(stage_a, stage_b, sep = " vs. "),
        .before = 1
      )
  }
)
```

```{r}
    fill = process
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.5,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(
      accuracy = 1
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Contribution to total dissimilarity",
    fill = NULL,
    title = "B. Relative contributions to network change"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 20,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

stage_overall_data <- stage_beta_pairwise_plot |>
  dplyr::select(
    comparison,
    beta_s,
    beta_wn
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(beta_s, beta_wn),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "dissimilarity"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = dplyr::recode(
      metric,
      beta_s = "Taxonomic dissimilarity (\u03b2S)",
      beta_wn = "Interaction-network dissimilarity (\u03b2WN)"
    )
  )

p_stage_overall <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  stage_overall_data,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = comparison,
    y = dissimilarity,
    group = metric,
    shape = metric
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Jaccard dissimilarity",
    shape = NULL,
    title = "C. Taxonomic and interaction dissimilarity",
    subtitle = "\u03b2S is shown separately because it is not part of the additive partition"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 20,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

```


# 5. Exploratory Bd branch

Bd is retained because the analyses are methodologically informative, but it is not currently integrated tightly enough with H1–H3 to serve as a main paper pillar.

## 5.1 Stage 8 — Initial Bd summaries and pooled host-node overlay

**Status:** Supporting/descriptive.

```{r bd-stage-08-summaries}

bd_clean <- bd %>%
  transmute(
    site_code = site,
    year,
    spp_code,
    bd_positive = bd_infect,
    bd_load = ave_ze_new
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # convert to logical
    bd_positive = case_when(
      bd_positive %in% c("Y", "YES", "Positive", 1, TRUE) ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    ),
    
    bd_load = as.numeric(bd_load)
    
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(spp_code)
  )

#host x site x year summaries
bd_host_site_year <- bd_clean %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(spp_code),
    !is.na(site_code),
    !is.na(year)
  ) %>%
  group_by(spp_code, site_code, year) %>%
  summarize(
    # Only swabs with a recorded infection result enter prevalence
    n_swabbed = sum(!is.na(bd_positive)),

    n_positive = sum(
      bd_positive == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    prevalence = if_else(
      n_swabbed > 0,
      n_positive / n_swabbed,
      NA_real_
    ),

    # Descriptive load summaries; intensity is modeled individually later
    mean_load = if (
      all(is.na(bd_load))
    ) NA_real_ else mean(bd_load, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_load = if (
      all(is.na(bd_load))
    ) NA_real_ else median(bd_load, na.rm = TRUE),

    max_load = if (
      all(is.na(bd_load))
    ) NA_real_ else max(bd_load, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

#aggregate to species level
bd_host_summary <- bd_host_site_year %>%
  group_by(spp_code) %>%
  summarize(
    total_swabbed = sum(n_swabbed),
    prevalence = weighted.mean(prevalence, w = n_swabbed, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_load = weighted.mean(mean_load, w = n_swabbed, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_load = median(median_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_load = max(max_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#bd summaries only on pooled host nodes
host_node_bd <- meta_node_summary %>%
  filter(node_type == "Host") %>%

host_node_bd %>%

  )


#rank by centrality

host_node_bd %>%

host_node_bd %>%

  ggplot(
```

## 5.2 Stage 9.5 — Standardize unequal swab totals

**Status:** Supporting sensitivity analysis. This is repeated subsampling/standardization rather than the primary inferential model.

```{r bd-stage-095-standardization}
# STAGE 9.5: Rarefaction of Bd data
set.seed(6262026)

# Number of swabs per species
bd_clean %>%
  count(spp_code)

# Smallest sample size
network_hosts <- c("BUBO", "PSRE", "RACA", "TAGR", "TATO")

bd_network <- bd_clean %>%
  filter(spp_code %in% network_hosts)

bd_network %>%
  count(spp_code)

min_n <- bd_network %>%
  count(spp_code) %>%
  summarize(min_n = min(n)) %>%
  pull()

min_n

rarefy_species <- function(df_species, sample_size){
  
  sampled <- df_species %>%
    slice_sample(n = sample_size)
  
  tibble(
    
    prevalence =
      mean(sampled$bd_positive),
    
    mean_load =
      mean(sampled$bd_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    median_load =
      median(sampled$bd_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    max_load =
      max(sampled$bd_load, na.rm = TRUE)
    
  )
}

#repeat 1000
n_iter <- 1000

bd_rarefied <- map_dfr(
  1:n_iter,
  function(i){
    bd_network %>%
      group_by(spp_code) %>%
      group_modify(~rarefy_species(.x, min_n)) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(iteration = i)
  }
  
)

bd_rarefied_summary <- bd_rarefied %>%
  
  group_by(spp_code) %>%
  
  summarize(
    
    prevalence_mean =
      mean(prevalence),
    
    prevalence_sd =
      sd(prevalence),
    
    prevalence_lower =
      quantile(prevalence, 0.025),
    
    prevalence_upper =
      quantile(prevalence, 0.975),
    
    mean_load_mean =
      mean(mean_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_load_sd =
      sd(mean_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_load_lower =
      quantile(mean_load, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    mean_load_upper =
      quantile(mean_load, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    median_load_mean =
      mean(median_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    max_load_mean =
      mean(max_load, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bd_rarefied_summary

bd_comparison <- bd_host_summary %>%
  
  select(
    spp_code,
    total_swabbed,
    prevalence,
    mean_load
  ) %>%
  
  left_join(
    bd_rarefied_summary,
    by = "spp_code"
  )

bd_comparison

ggplot(
  bd_rarefied_summary,
  aes(
    x = spp_code,
    y = prevalence_mean
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +

ggplot(

host_projection_bd <- host_projection_centrality %>%

host_projection_bd

```

### Retained interpretation

- RACA had moderate parasite sharing but the highest raw/standardized prevalence.
- TATO shared parasites broadly yet had the lowest prevalence.
- TATO had an extreme Bd-load outlier that distorted arithmetic load summaries.
- Projected hosts had similar strengths because the pooled projection was highly connected.

## 5.3 Stage 9.6 — Log-scale Bd load sensitivity

**Status:** Supporting sensitivity analysis.

```{r bd-stage-096-log-load}
# STAGE 9.6: Log-transform Bd load before rarefaction
set.seed(6262026)

# bd_load is right-skewed (see TATO outlier above) - log1p keeps zeros defined
bd_network <- bd_network %>%
  mutate(
    log_bd_load = log1p(bd_load)
  )

rarefy_species_log <- function(df_species, sample_size){

  sampled <- df_species %>%
    slice_sample(n = sample_size)

}

bd_rarefied_log <- map_dfr(

)

    max_log_load_mean =

bd_rarefied_log_summary
```

## 5.4 Stage 18 — Two-part Bd model

**Status:** Supporting/deprioritized. This is the cleanest Bd model currently available: infection occurrence is separated from intensity conditional on infection.

```{r bd-stage-18-two-part}
# STAGE 18: Model Bd using numerator/denominator directly, and split
# infection probability from infection intensity, rather than modeling
# an arithmetic site-year mean load (Stage 9.5/9.6's rarefaction stays
# useful as a sensitivity check, but isn't the primary inferential model)

bd_model_df <- bd_env_df %>%
  mutate(
    n_negative = n_swabbed - n_positive,
    site_year = interaction(site_code, year, drop = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  left_join(bullfrog_survey_status, by = c("site_code", "year")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bullfrog_detected))

# site-year prevalence - weights precision by n_swabbed properly, unlike
# treating every site-year's rarefied prevalence as equally informative
m_bd_prevalence_additive <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(n_positive, n_negative) ~
    bullfrog_detected +
    longevity +
    scale(log1p(pond_area_m)) +
    scale(max_depth_m) +
    ever_dry +
    spp_code +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code) +
    (1 | site_year),
  family = betabinomial,
  data = bd_model_df
)

summary(m_bd_prevalence_additive)

# individual-level two-part model: does infection occur, and if so, how
# intense (replaces treating raw/log mean load as the only load metric)
bd_occurrence_focal <- bd_clean %>%
  filter(
    spp_code %in% c("BUBO", "PSRE", "RACA", "TAGR", "TATO"),
    !is.na(bd_positive)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    spp_code = relevel(factor(spp_code), ref = "BUBO")
  )

m_bd_occurrence <- glmmTMB(
  bd_positive ~
    spp_code +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = binomial,
  data = bd_occurrence_focal
)

summary(m_bd_occurrence)

m_bd_intensity <- glmmTMB(
  bd_load ~
    spp_code +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = lognormal(),
  data = bd_clean %>%
    filter(bd_positive == 1, bd_load > 0)
)

summary(m_bd_intensity)
```

### Current interpretation

- Bd differed strongly among host species, but there was little evidence for broad temporal or pond-level effects.
- Relative to BUBO, PSRE, TAGR, and TATO had significantly lower individual infection probabilities in the focal-host model; RACA did not differ clearly.
- TAGR and TATO showed lower conditional intensity in the fitted output, although the original note highlighted TATO most strongly.
- Environmental factors and year generally did not predict Bd prevalence, occurrence, or intensity.


## 5.5 H4 Prediction

```{r}
# H4: does macroparasite-network position correspond to Bd infection risk?
# tested against BOTH Bd metrics, since "position corresponds to risk"
# shouldn't depend on which Bd outcome happens to get used

local_projection_centrality <- hp_edges %>%
  group_by(site_code, year) %>%
  group_modify(function(df, keys) {
    if (n_distinct(df$spp_code) < 3) return(tibble())
    projection <- build_host_jaccard_projection(df)
    g <- projection$graph
    tibble(
      spp_code = igraph::V(g)$name,
      local_strength = igraph::strength(g, weights = igraph::E(g)$jaccard),
      local_parasite_richness = igraph::V(g)$parasite_richness
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# parasites per individual - macroparasite burden proxy, parallel to bd_load
parasites_per_indiv <- hp_edges %>%
  group_by(site_code, year, spp_code) %>%
  summarize(
    total_parasites = sum(total_parasites, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_hosts_examined = max(n_hosts_examined, na.rm = TRUE),
    parasites_per_host = total_parasites / n_hosts_examined,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bd_local_network <- bd_host_site_year %>%
  left_join(local_projection_centrality, by = c("site_code", "year", "spp_code")) %>%
  left_join(parasites_per_indiv, by = c("site_code", "year", "spp_code")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(local_strength))

# model 1: Bd prevalence as the outcome (weights by n_swabbed properly)
m_bd_prevalence_local <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(n_positive, n_swabbed - n_positive) ~
    scale(local_strength) +
    scale(local_parasite_richness) +
    spp_code +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = betabinomial,
  data = bd_local_network
)

summary(m_bd_prevalence_local)

# model 2: Bd load as the outcome - continuous, conditional on a positive mean
m_bd_load_local <- glmmTMB(
  mean_load ~
    scale(local_strength) +
    scale(local_parasite_richness) +
    spp_code +
    scale(year) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = lognormal(),
  data = bd_local_network %>% filter(mean_load > 0)
)

summary(m_bd_load_local)

# the detailed comparison: does centrality's association with Bd flip sign
# or significance depending on which Bd metric is used?
tibble(
  outcome = c("prevalence", "load"),
  local_strength_estimate = c(
    fixef(m_bd_prevalence_local)$cond[["scale(local_strength)"]],
    fixef(m_bd_load_local)$cond[["scale(local_strength)"]]
  )
)
```

- RACA as the std of comparison





### Decision for the network paper

Retain at most one final local site-year network-position test. If local macroparasite position does not predict Bd, report that negative boundary result briefly and close this branch rather than expanding additional Bd models.





# 6. Deprioritized or superseded analyses

These blocks are retained so that exploratory work and written interpretations are not lost, but they are excluded from the active workflow. They are set to `eval=FALSE`.

## 6.1 Stage 6 — Bullfrog status inferred from `hp_edges`

**Status:** Superseded by independent survey-based `bullfrog_detected`. Absence from parasite records cannot establish biological absence.

```{r archive-stage-06-bullfrog, eval=FALSE}
#stage 6: bullfrog presence - absence

bullfrog <- "RACA"
bullfrog_site_years <- hp_edges %>%
  distinct(site_code, year, spp_code) %>%
  group_by(site_code, year) %>%
  summarize(
    bullfrog_present = any(spp_code == bullfrog),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bullfrog_site_years %>%
  count(bullfrog_present)

#adding bullfrog presence status to all edges 
hp_edges_bf <- hp_edges %>%
  left_join(
    bullfrog_site_years,
    by = c("site_code", "year")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    bullfrog_present = replace_na(bullfrog_present, FALSE),
    bullfrog_status = if_else(
      bullfrog_present,
      "Bullfrog present",
      "Bullfrog absent"
    )
  )

hp_edges_bf %>%
  count(bullfrog_status)

#building present/absent networks 
bf_present_net <- build_subset_network(
  data = hp_edges_bf %>% filter(bullfrog_present),
  subset_type = "bullfrog_status",
  subset_value = "present"
)

bf_absent_net <- build_subset_network(
  data = hp_edges_bf %>% filter(!bullfrog_present),
  subset_type = "bullfrog_status",
  subset_value = "absent"
)


#network level comparison
bullfrog_network_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarize_hp_graph(
    g = bf_present_net$graph,
    subset_type = "bullfrog_status",
    subset_value = "present"
  ),
  summarize_hp_graph(
    g = bf_absent_net$graph,
    subset_type = "bullfrog_status",
    subset_value = "absent"
```

## 6.3 Stage 16 — First GLMM pass

**Status:** Superseded by Stages 23–24. The richness dataset was conditioned on `n_parasites >= 3`, and the interaction should not be used without adequate bullfrog-by-longevity support.

```{r archive-stage-16-first-glmm, eval=FALSE}
# STAGE 16: Replace ordinary lm (Stage 9) with GLMMs that account for
# repeated measurement within site and use response-appropriate

network_df_model <- network_df %>%
  filter(!network_too_small)

# parasite richness - overdispersed count, site random effect, effort as
# a covariate (NOT an offset - richness doesn't scale proportionally with n)
m_richness <- glmmTMB(
  n_parasites ~
    bullfrog_present * longevity +
    scale(year) +
    scale(log1p(total_dissected)) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = poisson,
  data = network_df_model
)

summary(m_richness)

# connectance - realized links out of possible links, beta-binomial to
# absorb overdispersion a plain binomial can't
network_df_model <- network_df_model %>%
  mutate(
    possible_links = n_hosts * n_parasites,
    missing_links = possible_links - n_edges
  )

m_connectance <- glmmTMB(
  cbind(n_edges, missing_links) ~
    bullfrog_present * longevity +
    scale(year) +
    scale(log1p(total_dissected)) +
    (1 | site_code),
  family = betabinomial,
  data = network_df_model
)

summary(m_connectance)

network_df_model %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bullfrog_present, y = connectance)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = longevity), width = 0.1, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Bullfrog present (survey-based)",
    y = "Connectance",
    color = "Longevity",
    title = "Site-year connectance by bullfrog presence and longevity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
